scope: Theorem 4.2 (Uniform representing densities) of the manuscript “A negatively pinched Kähler threefold without bounded holomorphic coordinates” (preprints/A-negatively-pinched-Kahler-threefold-without-bounded-holomorphic-coordinates-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 359 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 59e7bcf19b96d5d9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant K∗ > 0, depending only on the fixed profiles f, b and R0, with the following property. For every fixed D0 > max{1, 2 √ 2R0} there is an integer threshold Q0 such that, for every integer Q ≥ Q0 and every choice of the separated sets above, the recursion (4.2) has the following properties for all j ≥ 1: 1. Wj is smooth and strictly positive, and Wj dσ represents holomorphic evaluation at zero. In particular it is a probability measure. 2. Under global phase rotation, Wj has frequencies only between −ℓj and ℓj, and its mean on every phase orbit is exactly one. 3. At every point of S, c0Wj−1 ≤ Wj ≤ 2Wj−1, |ZWj| ≤ K∗ q kj Wj, |TWj| ≤ K∗kjWj (4.3) for every unit horizontal vector Z. The threshold Q0 may also be enlarged to impose any fixed lower threshold on the degrees kj.
